subject: Post-call: deployment decision checklist & dedicated sizing clarifications
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Lucy Chen <lucy@acmeai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: deployment decision checklist & dedicated sizing clarifications

Hi Lucy — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can lock a recommended Dedicated capacity plan for AcmeAI.

What I heard on the call:
- Primary workload: real-time customer support completions for website chat and an internal summarization pipeline for support tickets.
- Peak expected storefront traffic: 1,200 requests/minute (bursts to 2k/min for promotions).
- Typical token mix: avg prompt ~120 tokens, avg completion ~420 tokens (so ~540 tokens per request).
- Target p95 latency: <= 220ms first-token for customer chat (preference), happy to balance for cheaper steady-state if needed.
- Security: prefer private VPC but open to Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering for initial pilot.

Clarifying questions to finalize a Dedicated config: 
1) Confirm target TPS (tokens/sec). From the numbers above I estimate ~10k tokens/sec steady, ~17k tokens/sec burst — can you confirm?
2) What percent of requests are streaming vs non-streaming? Streaming affects CPU/io and batching behavior.
3) Any requirement for on-prem/air-gapped deployment in the next 6–12 months?
4) Do you have a preferred GPU family? We typically recommend H100 for high-concurrency workloads and A100 for cost-optimized steady throughput. L4 is good for lower latency but smaller context.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- You answer the 4 questions above (1–2 short bullets each)
- We’ll produce a capacity worksheet with 2 scenarios: conservative (A100 80% reserved + burst H100) and performance (H100 primary), including projected token-unit cost and latency p95.
- If you confirm Dedicated, we’ll target a pilot contract (30–60 days) and schedule an ops deep-dive with your infra team.

I’ve attached a capacity worksheet template (filled with our initial estimates) and an example inference profile. Opening time for a 30-minute ops session next Tue/Wed?

Thanks — Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: acmeai_capacity_worksheet_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), example_inference_profile.json (text)

From: Lucy Chen <lucy@acmeai.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmeai.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 15:18:44 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment decision checklist & dedicated sizing clarifications

Thanks Vanessa — great summary. Answers inline: 

1) TPS (tokens/sec): steady-state ~9.5k tokens/sec, expected marketing burst windows up to ~19k tokens/sec for ~10–15 minutes, average daily 12 hours of peak activity.
2) Streaming: ~65% of chat requests are streamed (we show partial results as they generate), the internal summarization is non-streaming batch.
3) On-prem: not in the next 6 months. We may require full air-gapped/on-prem in 9–18 months for regulated customers, but not for the pilot.
4) GPU preference: no hard requirement, but infra prefers fewer H100s if latency gains are material. Cost sensitivity: team wants to avoid >10% increase in token-unit cost compared to our current baseline.

Also: context window required for the chat path is 6k tokens; summarization uses 32k. We can consider two model variants or a single larger-context model depending on price.

Happy to take the ops deep-dive next Wed May 26 10:00–10:30 PT.

—Lucy
Lucy Chen
Head of ML Platforms | AcmeAI
lucy@acmeai.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: deployment decision checklist & dedicated sizing clarifications (AcmeAI)

Folks — forwarding Lucy’s answers. Key bits: 9.5k steady tokens/sec, 19k burst, 65% streaming, chat context 6k / summarization 32k, pilot will not be on-prem. They’d prefer minimising cost delta vs current baseline.

My thinking for an initial Dedicated pilot: 
- Model strategy: run two model variants behind the same endpoint — a 6k-context model for chat (primary), and a 32k-context summarization model for batch. Route requests by path. This avoids larger-context GPUs all the time.
- GPU recommendation: start with a mixed pool: 6 x H100 (primary) + 4 x A100 (secondary/burst + summarization batch jobs). H100s handle high-concurrency streaming (lower p95). A100s are cheaper for sustained batch summarization.
- Estimated concurrency/throughput: with Redwood batching profile and KV cache, 6 H100s should handle ~11–14k tokens/sec steady for low-latency streaming; bursts to 20k tokens/sec should trigger autoscale to the A100 pool + short-lived H100 burst capacity.
- Token mix & cost: with this mix we estimate token-unit cost within ~8–10% of their baseline (meets their ask).

Questions for Karthik and Alex: 
- Does the mixed pool make sense operationally for Dedicated (routing, autoscale, fallbacks)?
- Any suggested change to counts (6/4) based on our existing kernel optimizations for 6k vs 32k contexts?

I’ll draft the capacity scenarios once you confirm.

—Vanessa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>, Lucy Chen <lucy@acmeai.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment decision checklist & dedicated sizing clarifications

Nice summary — appreciate the framing Vanessa. A few notes/adjustments: 

- Routing/ops: Mixed pool is fine; we should pin chat endpoints to H100-backed sub-pool with sticky routing for KV-cache locality. Summarization jobs should be scheduled onto the A100 pool with job-queueing for off-peak windows where possible. Autoscale policy: proactive scaling on queue depth + reactive on p95 latency.
- H100 count: bump to 8 H100s for safety on the pilot to avoid frequent burst scale-ups during initial tuning. We can scale down after 2 weeks of telemetry.
- A100 count: keep 4 but reserve 1 for longer 32k summarization batches to avoid interfering with throughput.
- Quantization: plan to test 4-bit quantization on summarization variant to lower A100 cost; keep chat on fp16 on H100 for latency/quality.
- Ops next steps: I’ll prepare a workload-runbook (start/stop, autoscale thresholds, fallback models) and attach to the capacity worksheet. Vanessa — please include a line item for a 2-week post-pilot performance review with telemetry export.

Lucy — if this matches your expectations we’ll update the workbook and send a pilot SOW and a calendar invite for the ops deep-dive.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
